svg.title: Three ways a fine-grained policy can leave Unity Catalog
svg.desc: Unity Catalog evaluates the policy. Cross-engine ABAC, generally available on 1 October 2026, sanitizes rows in a serverless filtering layer before an external engine sees them. Iceberg read restrictions hand nine masking actions and a row filter to a trusted engine, which must enforce them or fail. Catalog labels move key-value metadata to another catalog and do not enforce a decision.

g.text: Unity Catalog evaluates the policy for this principal
Tags, UDFs, TO, and EXCEPT stay in the catalog. The policy text does not travel.
What leaves depends on which door the reader is standing at.
Centralized enforcement
Cross-engine ABAC. GA in the 1 October release notes.
Documented client: Apache Spark, Delta or Iceberg.
A serverless layer filters and returns sanitized rows.
The external engine is not asked to mask anything.
Reads only, while a fine-grained policy applies.
A writer must be exempt from that policy.
Managed table, catalog commits, external data access.
OAuth machine-to-machine, or a personal access token.
Usage product: EXTERNAL_COMPATIBILITY.
This is the door for an engine the user controls.
DuckDB and Starburst are not in the October page.
Delegated enforcement
Iceberg read-restrictions on loadTable.
Spec. Not the October Databricks product page.
Nine masking actions, plus a row-filter predicate.
Columns are field ids, not names.
Filter the raw values, then apply the masks.
A reader that cannot apply one fails the query.
It must not return raw, partial, or empty rows.
Trust between catalog and engine is out of scope.
A client that ignores the object can read the files.
SQL UDFs and lookup subqueries do not fit.
Do not cache the response across principals.
Catalog labels, the third door
Key-value metadata on the table and on each field id. The spec lets a client ignore them.
A consuming catalog maps the pairs onto its own tags and enforces with its own policies.
No shared meaning is defined. A label does not mask a column by itself.
Use this door when the destination is another catalog, not when it is a Spark job.
The 10 September Databricks post is the map. The 1 October pages are the two contracts.
Inside Databricks is a fourth bill, not this feature
Dedicated-compute fine-grained access control is FINE_GRAINED_ACCESS_CONTROL.
A SQL warehouse query is not cross-engine ABAC. Do not add the two usage lines together.
